<!-- pr-reviewer: ae9d556cb83adccd51a62d3397096db6fb370436 -->
**Verdict: Needs a branch refresh before merge. The review found no code defects, but the PR conflicts with current `main`.**

Thank you @ivisaf - this is a careful post, and the Z-lift rethink in the last commit is exactly the kind of safety call this project wants.

**What looks good**
- Provenance: the `grblhal.cps` header and `docs/decisions/710-grblhal-post.md` cite only grblHAL's public core README, the LinuxCNC G-code reference and RS-274. The author states the GPL source was not read. I found no HSMWorks/Fusion post text, output or assets, and the goldens are produced by the post itself.
- Refusals by name, each with a counted `message()`: control/wear compensation (`onRadiusCompensation`), tapping G84 (`grblhal.cps:~420`, once per program), tilted moves (`tiltOk`), go-home after an operation, and probing (no probe hook, so the engine refuses). An unknown or buried Z-lift height is refused by name in `liftRefuse` (`grblhal.cps:~242`) rather than guessed. I found no silent wrong output.
- Declining to emit G43/G43.1/G49 is reasoned in the decision file, and it is a defensible departure from the issue text.
- The safe-retract logic (`G53` only when the machine states `safe_retract`, otherwise a work-offset lift above stock) is the safe reading for unhomed `$22=0` machines. The generic machine states none, which is consistent.
- Decision file present, `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #710` in the body, no `CHANGELOG.md` edits, no new dependency and no `build.rs`/`.github`/scripts changes. The Rust changes are only the registry lines in `posting.rs` and a doc string in `script/mod.rs`, with no `unwrap`/`expect`.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` and README are updated alongside the post.

**Local results** (PR head `ae9d556c`, tested unmerged because of the conflict below; debug)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| conformance | 6 passed |
| grblhal_post | 9 passed |
| fanuc_post | 11 passed |
| inverted_post | 15 passed |
| after_op | 10 passed |
| coolant | 7 passed |
| coolant_followups | 7 passed |
| comment_escape | 3 passed |
| control_comp | 5 passed |
| wear_comp | 5 passed |
| machine | 32 passed |
| posting | 17 passed |
| camcraft-post `comp` | 9 passed |
| `clippy -p camcraft-app --lib -- -D warnings` | clean |

Whole-crate `cargo test --no-run` stops at `lathe_thread_travel.rs` (`missing field hand in OpParams`). The PR does not touch that file, as you noted, so it is not held against this PR. The UI lib filters (`machines_pane`, `post`) were not re-run by me.

**Requested before merge**
1. Refresh the branch (`git merge upstream/main`). There are two small additive conflicts. In `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (the `MACHINES` list, ~line 147) and `crates/app/tests/machine.rs` (`every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks`, ~line 744), `main` added the Tormach 8L, 15L Slant-PRO and 15LX Slant-PRO lathes beside your `grblHAL 3-axis` entry. Keep both sides, and keep the order the same in the two places, because the test zips `MACHINES` against its expectation list. Then re-run `machine`, `posting` and `conformance`, since the machine-list ordering is what they pin.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
- `grblhal.cps` comment on canned cycles lists G85, but `onCycle` never emits it. Either map it or drop it from the comment.
- The Setup pane's End-units row still shows only for Tormach, as you noted. Fine as a follow-up.
- The PR is not a draft. If you still plan changes, `gh pr ready 715 --undo` keeps it clear of a premature merge.

**Not exercised**
Nothing here ran on a real grblHAL controller or simulator, and I could not run it on a Hub. The goldens only prove that the post's text is stable and matches its tests, not that the controller accepts it. Anyone with a grblHAL machine is welcome to dry-run it (Z raised, no stock, hand on feed hold) and report on #710, especially the Z lift before each tool change and at the end.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
